final_text:
Using the species-level rows (rank S) with at least 10 clade reads, 6 of the 10 spiked organisms are detected and 4 are missed.

| Organism | Species clade reads | Result |
|---|---|---|
| pseudomonas aeruginosa | 811 | detected |
| escherichia coli | 72 | detected |
| lactobacillus fermentum (reported as Limosilactobacillus fermentum) | 26 | detected |
| enterococcus faecalis | 6457 | detected |
| staphylococcus aureus | 54 | detected |
| salmonella enterica | 4 | missed (below 10) |
| bacillus subtilis | 2 | missed (below 10) |
| listeria monocytogenes | no species row | missed |
| saccharomyces cerevisiae | not in the report | missed |
| cryptococcus neoformans | not in the report | missed |

For Listeria, the report has only a genus-level row (315 reads), so *Listeria monocytogenes* has no species-level count. The Bacillus subtilis group row (11 reads) is a different clade from the species row, so I used the species count of 2.

RESULT: {"detected": ["pseudomonas aeruginosa", "escherichia coli", "lactobacillus fermentum", "enterococcus faecalis", "staphylococcus aureus"], "missed": ["salmonella enterica", "listeria monocytogenes", "bacillus subtilis", "saccharomyces cerevisiae", "cryptococcus neoformans"]}

I listed five organisms as missed in the RESULT line, although the table above shows only four rows marked "missed". Salmonella enterica, Bacillus subtilis, Listeria, Saccharomyces and Cryptococcus are the five that fail, and so the correct split is 5 detected and 5 mi
